messages:
Maria K: FYI customer reported a hole in their SIEM for 2029-04-03 02:00-03:00 UTC — events present in raw S3 but not showing in their Splunk timebucket.
SRE Oncall: I pulled the forwarder logs, saw repeated warnings: "time_bucket_mismatch: event_ts=2029-04-03T02:12:40Z bucket_label=2029-04-03T01:00:00Z". Appears the forwarder assigned the wrong bucket occasionally.
Tom D: That sounds like the local timezone->UTC rounding bug we fixed last quarter? But that was in the partitioning code, not the SIEM forwarder.
Rohan S: I can repro locally with the same backlog export flags. Running the forwarder with --batch-window 60s and a synthetic event stream causes bucket rollover to shift by -1h when an event crosses DST-like boundary in our partition math.
Maria K: Customer is on Splunk HEC ingest. They say the missing hour corresponds to a single export job run at 02:00 UTC.
SRE Oncall: audit-forwarder-bot posted an error during that run: 

```
ERROR forwarder/shipper.go:239 timebucket mismatch: computed=2029-04-03T01:00:00Z event=2029-04-03T02:12:40Z batch_id=export-20290403-02
```

Tom D: Can you paste the exact forwarder command that ran? Need flags + version.
SRE Oncall: From deploy logs: `./audit-forwarder --export-prefix customer-123 --target siem --batch-window=60 --version=2.4.1` deployed at 2029-04-03T02:00:05Z.
Rohan S: Version 2.4.1 has a known edge-case with minute-level batching and cross-day sequence numbers. I patched it in 2.4.3. Could be the culprit.
Maria K: Customer asked if this is a data-loss event or just indexing delay. What's the status of the files on S3?
SRE Oncall: Files present in S3 under `s3://audit-exports/customer-123/2029/04/03/02/` — I downloaded sample file; events are in there but each event has an envelope field `time_bucket` set to `2029-04-03T01:00:00Z`.
Ana P: If the events are in S3, Splunk can reindex them if we re-run the forwarder with corrected bucket assignment. Need to confirm KMS metadata is present before reforwarding.
SRE Oncall: Quick check: for the problematic files, `kms_info` is present but `kms_key_id` is null for a few older objects — maybe rotation race. Example metadata dump: {"kms_info":{},"checksum":"abc123"}.
Tom D: Hmm — two separate issues then: (A) buggy bucket calc in 2.4.1, (B) spotty kms_key_id missing for objects created during rotation window. Missing kms_key_id might break our re-encrypt/forward pipeline.
Rohan S: Repro steps I used locally:
```
# generate synthetic events spanning the boundary
python tools/gen_audit.py --start 2029-04-03T01:59:00Z --end 2029-04-03T02:02:00Z --rate 500/s > events.ndjson
# run forwarder at the same binary + flags
./audit-forwarder --dry-run --batch-window=60 --input events.ndjson --version 2.4.1 | grep time_bucket
```
I see time_bucket slip by -1h for ~0.6% of events.
Maria K: Good repro. What's the mitigation for the customer now?
Ana P: Short term we can: (1) re-run the forwarder on those S3 objects using fixed binary (2.4.3) in dry-run to confirm buckets are recomputed correctly, (2) if kms_key_id missing, run metadata-repair job to reattach kms_key_id from backup, then reforward.
SRE Oncall: I ran a local metadata-repair simulation: `./meta-repair --bucket audit-exports --prefix customer-123/2029/04/03/02 --fix-kms`. It reports 27 objects with null kms_key_id and claims to reattach using previous key mapping.
Tom D: Important: don't change object encryption in-place. The repair should only attach metadata pointers we store in the export manifest. If not present, we must backfill from WAL.
Rohan S: I'll prepare a safe reforward plan and a backfill script. Plan outline: `1) lock export job for customer-123; 2) run meta-repair dry-run; 3) run forwarder v2.4.3 in dry-run to validate buckets; 4) schedule live reforward with rate limiting; 5) provide Splunk HEC replay token to customer.`
Maria K: Customer wants ETA. Can we promise a same-day fix?
Ana P: If meta-repair is straightforward we can reforward today evening UTC. If we need WAL backfill that could be 24-48h.
SRE Oncall: I'll start meta-repair dry-run now and post results here in ~30m.
Tom D: Also include a short postmortem draft mentioning: root cause = bucket calc bug in 2.4.1 + edge KMS metadata race during rotation; remediation = patch forwarder (released 2.4.3), add integration test for cross-boundary events, make metadata-repair idempotent, stronger KMS rotation handshake.
Maria K: Please @Ana P when you have confirmation so we can tell the customer. Also can we send the temporary Splunk reindex instructions?
Ana P: Copying a quick reindex snippet for Splunk HEC team:
```
# sample CLI to POST ndjson to HEC
curl -k -H "Authorization: Splunk <token>" --data-binary @events.ndjson https://splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector
```
I'll format and send to customer once we validate dry-run.
SRE Oncall: meta-repair dry-run results: 27 objects affected, all solvable via manifest mapping. No re-encryption required. Dry-run of forwarder v2.4.3 on samples recomputes time_bucket correctly.
Maria K: Great. Next steps and owners: Rohan S -> run live meta-repair + reforward tonight; Tom D -> add regression test and schedule 2.4.3 rollout; Ana P -> notify customer and provide reindex instructions; SRE Oncall -> monitor splunk ingest and confirm.
